protected_passages.passage: His example puts status and hidden need in one sentence: "I was the king of my school and I don't have a yearbook because it was $35 and I just wouldn't ask them for that much money."
One GQ exchange cuts both ways. Retiring early to a ranch to hunt birds, he said, was "what I secretly want to do."
That is common audition advice. What stands out is how long Pratt was better at the selling than the job.
A Three can sincerely want a quieter life while living a louder one, and he still calls his career a very high priority.
What happened next matters most for typing, because no camera was involved.

It is also the 2015 move in reverse. Eleven years after "Now I have less fun. I focus more," the fun is back on the plan, chosen in a meeting by a man who learned as a teenage salesman that the attitude is part of what you sell.
